title: A volunteer fire department that has just had its first responder shortage

scenario.title: A volunteer fire department that has just had its first responder shortage
scenario.setting: A volunteer fire department that has just had its first responder shortage

characters.name: Steward
characters.tendencies: Tends the canon of the place.

characters.name: Counter

turns.name: Steward
turns.text:
I just double-checked the current responder rosters and found we’re short eight trained firefighters and two paramedics for the overnight shift. We can’t ask the small crew that’s left to cover both day and night assignments without risking serious burnout.
[grabs a stack of neon yellow volunteer sign-up sheets from the front counter and tapes them to the fire engine’s side panel and the station’s front glass door]

turns.name: Counter
turns.text:
"We’re stuck with a massive staffing gap after this week’s first responder shortage, and I’m asking anyone who can spare a shift or training hour to sign up before we field the next emergency call. I know most of us have been working double shifts for days straight, but we can’t leave our town unprotected for the next structure fire or medical incident."
[Pins a stack of volunteer sign-up sheets to the station’s cork noticeboard, adjusting the frayed fire department flag taped to its edge first.]

turns.name: Apprentice
turns.text:
Folks, we just got word three more of our regular crew members bailed right after that last structure fire, leaving us dangerously shorthanded for all upcoming shifts. I’ve got stacks of volunteer sign-up sheets set up by the kitchen coffee pot, and we’ll train anyone willing to help with everything from hose work to rehab support on-site absolutely free.
[Grabs a chipped fire department coffee mug to gesture toward the crumpled sign-up sheets stacked on the nearby counter, a furrowed, urgent brow as he scans the quiet station bay for anyone willing to step up.]

turns.name: Steward
turns.text:
I already crunched the updated staffing numbers after the apprentice’s update—we’re now short 11 trained firefighters and four paramedics for the overnight shift. I’ve pulled our standby cross-trained volunteer roster, and we have enough on-call responders to fill the gap, but I need to lock in their confirmations right now before the 10 PM handoff deadline.
[Grabs the wall-mounted CB radio, flips to the volunteer emergency channel, and leans in to press the talk button to broadcast the urgent shift request.]

turns.name: Counter
turns.text:
"We’re stuck with a massive staffing gap after this week’s first responder shortage, and I was just about to ask anyone who can spare a shift or training hour to step forward—until now learning three more of our regular crew bailed right after that last fire? That’s catastrophic. I’m sticking through the entire overnight shift myself, and anyone with even basic fire response training needs to grab a sign-up sheet right now.
[Slamming a fist against the metal edge of the dispatch desk then snatching a crumpled stack of printed volunteer sign-up forms off the counter and holding the stack out to the small group of remaining firefighters clustered near the station’s fire engine bays.

turns.name: Apprentice
turns.text:
Folks, we just got word three more of our regular crew members bailed right after that last structure fire, leaving us dangerously shorthanded for all overnight and morning patrol shifts. I know most of our regular volunteers have already picked up double shifts this week, but we can’t leave this community uncovered for a single moment. If you have even a few free hours to fill a shift or help orient our new certified cadets, please come forward to sign up now.
[Grabs a stack of blank shift sign-up sheets from the dispatch counter and pins a few to the station’s main bulletin board for anyone passing by to grab.]

dm_opening: DM opening: the cast gathers around a question the scene has been carrying for a year.
